requestDemoPage.title: Nesto is open
requestDemoPage.body: Nesto is available today as a platform for construction companies — anyone in construction can join.
requestDemoPage.whatItCovers: Architects, engineers, project managers, contractors and other professionals can create an independent profile in minutes. Running a construction company and want a full workspace? Reach out and we'll set one up with you directly.

contactPage.title: Contact Nesto
contactPage.intro: Have a question, want to see the platform, or need to report a security concern? Here's how to reach us.
contactPage.supportBody: Account, workspace or billing questions — we typically reply within one business day.
contactPage.salesBody: Want to see Nesto in action, or apply for a company workspace?
contactPage.securityBody: Found a security issue, or want to understand our tenant isolation and access model?

securityPage.title: Security
securityPage.intro: Nesto is built as a private operating system for a single construction company at a time. Every workspace's data lives behind its own tenant boundary — here is what that means concretely, in the system as it exists today.
securityPage.isolationBody: Every record — projects, tasks, clients, documents, comments — is scoped to a tenant ID at the data layer. A user session is bound to one tenant; there is no query path that lets one company's workspace read another's.
securityPage.authBody: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt before storage — Nesto never stores or logs a plaintext password. Sessions are signed tokens verified on every request, and login responses are shaped identically whether or not an account exists, so a failed attempt can't be used to guess valid usernames.
securityPage.accessBody: There is no public self-registration. Every account is created by a Company Admin or Owner inside the workspace, and access can be suspended or archived by them at any time without deleting the underlying history.
securityPage.permissionsBody: Every department (Finance, HR, Legal, Architecture, Sales and more) has its own permission level per resource — read, write, or full — enforced on both the interface and the server action handling the request, not just hidden in the UI.

forgotPassword.title: Forgot your password?
